item.title: China pushes toward task-oriented AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
China is accelerating efforts to turn advances in artificial intelligence into a vital driver of economic growth as technology companies and manufacturers use AI models to develop new products and improve productivity. Discussions at the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit highlighted three areas shaping this transition: the growing role of open-source models in expanding access to AI, the integration of AI into industrial operations, and the development of robots capable of performing physical tasks. Together, they not only point to opportunities for Chinese companies in software, manufacturing and services, but also underline the challenges of controlling costs, ensuring reliability and making the technology commercially viable. Held from Nov 2 to 5 in Wuzhen, Zhejiang province, the WIC Wuzhen Summit brought together technology executives, researchers and policymakers to discuss the development and governance of AI. Zhang Yaqin, founding dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for AI Industry Research, said AI is moving toward a new stage in which intelligent agents could perform tasks across industries, scientific research and biology. He also envisaged an internet in which AI agents interact with one another. China has a substantial industrial base to support this transition. The country's core AI industry was valued at more than 1.2 trillion yuan ($180 billion) in 2025, while the number of AI companies exceeded 6,600 as of June 2026, according to the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, a research institute under the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Zhu Keli, founding director of the China Institute of New Economy, said competition in AI is expanding beyond model development to include industry-specific applications, data and business ecosystems. Companies are increasingly focused on computing efficiency and sustainable revenue, making access to customers, industry expertise and the ability to integrate AI into existing operations critical to commercial success. International cooperation is one way to bring these capabilities together. In a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the summit on Nov 3, Premier Li Qiang highlighted the nation's commitment to working with other countries to build an open, inclusive and dynamic digital innovation ecosystem. Li said China will continue to embrace open innovation and promote technology transfer and knowledge sharing. He underlined the need to adhere to inclusive and balanced development of the internet to allow digital dividends to be shared.

item.title: When in Shanghai, they speak Shanghainese
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
When Serbian Filip Filipovic said "liang nianji" instead of the standard Mandarin "er nianji" — both referring to the second grade — in a video, someone posted a comment to correct him. Shanghai viewers quickly jumped to his defense: He grew up in Shanghai. That's how we say it, they noted. For Filipovic, who speaks Mandarin with a strong Shanghai accent, the episode revealed how deeply the city had shaped him. While on tours in northern China, compliments on his fluent Chinese are often followed by a question: "You learned it in the south, didn't you?" Overseas, his Shanghainese greetings put his fellow conference participants from Shanghai at ease instantly. Such encounters reflect Shanghai's international character. The city recorded 7.139 million new temporary accommodation registrations by foreign nationals in 2025, up 49.6 percent year-on-year, according to the municipal public security bureau. Filipovic's earliest teacher was the television. Watching local programs, he listened to the Shanghainese being spoken and began imitating the way of talking. Stand-up comedy came next, particularly performances by Seven, a popular comedian. Filipovic then added Duolingo to his learning routine, describing its new Shanghainese course as "structured catch-up learning". He estimates that he understands 70 to 80 percent of the comedy programs he now watches, guessing the rest from context. Language-learning app Duolingo launched its Shanghainese course on Oct 15. Lessons introduce phrases for situations ranging from workplace conversations to dating and everyday encounters. Belgian jazz musician Tobias Le Compte began learning the dialect in Belgium in 2021, after watching the Shanghainese-dialect film B for Busy. He was so serious about learning that he directed friends to send him voice messages in the dialect. Anyone who slipped into Mandarin would owe him a meal. "I thought if I were in Shanghai, being able to speak Shanghainese might help me understand the city better," he said. At the Chengjiaqiao Community Cultural Activity Center in Changning district, local residents now gather to watch Compte perform the kind of comedy he once studied online. He appears in Hu Shang Fan Ren Ge, a comedy organized by the Shanghai Oriental Publicity and Education Service Center. Set in a residential community, the production brings together locals, newcomers and foreigners through stories about deliveries, waste sorting and neighbors helping one another. His learning experience has also inspired others. When he arrived in Shanghai in 2023, people recognized him at the airport. Some parents told him his videos had encouraged their children to speak Shanghainese again. Shi Menghui, an assistant to the head of Fudan University's Department of Chinese Language and Literature, welcomed the role played by foreign residents in popularizing Shanghainese. Non-native speakers can notice differences that native speakers don't, Shi said, citing British missionary Joseph Edkins' 1853 compilation of the dialect's grammar as a valuable record. "A dialect's vitality depends not only on the number of speakers, but also on how frequently it is used in public, the settings in which it is spoken and its symbolic value," Shi said. The interest also reflects Shanghai's cultural appeal, Shi added. Serbian resident Filipovic hopes more international residents will try speaking the dialect, starting with "nong ho" — the local way to say hello. "Shanghai is an international metropolis. Being international and learning the local language are not contradictory," he said.

item.title: APEC growth forecast upgraded to 3.4 percent
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
The economy of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation region is projected to grow 3.4 percent in 2026, supported by strong technology investments even as energy costs and trade restrictions weigh on the outlook. "We have a combination of upside opportunities but also downside risks," said Carlos Kuriyama, director of the APEC Policy Support Unit. Speaking at an online media briefing held on Sunday by the APEC Secretariat ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, which will be held on Wednesday and Thursday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, Kuriyama said that regional economic growth has remained resilient, but the economic environment is becoming more challenging. The latest growth forecast is higher than the earlier projection of 3.2 percent, according to the report released by the APEC Policy Support Unit on Sunday. Trade in goods has provided a significant boost. In the first half of 2026, the export values of all APEC member economies combined surged 22.5 percent year-on-year, compared with 6.5 percent a year earlier. While the trade outlook for this year is relatively good, Kuriyama said that he expects a moderation in the growth of export and import volume over the next two years, due to economic challenges, supply chain restrictions and trade policy uncertainty. Inflation is also expected to increase to 3.2 percent in 2026, up 0.8 percentage point from 2025, driven by higher energy prices and electricity costs. "Based on the current situation, we are advocating … for policy priorities," said Kuriyama, stressing the need for an effective mix of monetary and fiscal policy, diversifying investments and energy sources, strengthening the trade environment and fortifying multilateral links. Also at the media briefing, Eduardo Pedrosa, executive director of the APEC Secretariat, said that building resilience is a key focus of this year's APEC discussions. Under China's rotating chairmanship, APEC has set openness, innovation and cooperation as priorities. Pedrosa noted that APEC economies represent more than 60 percent of global GDP, and that roughly 300 meetings have been held this year, including a trade ministers' meeting in May in Suzhou, Jiangsu province. "I think what makes APEC unique is that we are a process," said Pedrosa, adding that APEC provides a platform for regional economic leaders and the business community, enabling member economies to engage. kelly@chinadailyapac.com

item.title: Shenzhen ready to welcome Asia-Pacific leaders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
At the APEC media center in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Saturday, Russia Today journalist Mariia Cherdantseva watched a robot prepare coffee — a sight that she had expected in a city often dubbed "China's Silicon Valley". Having previously visited Shenzhen, Cherdantseva said that she is impressed every time by how the city has developed. She found the center's artificial intelligence applications both useful for journalists and fun to interact with. The media center, which opened on Nov 11 for journalists covering the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Week, offers a glimpse into the city's preparations for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on Wednesday and Thursday. Shenzhen will become the third Chinese city to host the event, after Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. This year's meeting is themed "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", with openness, innovation and cooperation as priorities. The city's preparations extend well beyond the media center, bringing together conference arrangements, visitor services and technology to welcome guests from across the Asia-Pacific. At a news briefing on Saturday, Shenzhen Mayor Li Yun said that all of the meeting venues were ready following equipment checks and full rehearsals. Dedicated channels for delegates have been established at nine ports of entry spanning sea, land, air and rail routes. Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport has introduced advanced screening technology for checked baggage in order to streamline clearance, Li said. More than 100,000 foreign-language signs have been standardized across the city, and over 7,000 AI translation devices have been installed at transport hubs, tourist attractions and shopping areas. Visitors can use bank cards issued overseas to pay for metro rides or withdraw cash from more than 3,000 ATMs across the city, while 1,360 conference volunteers and tens of thousands of city volunteers are on hand to help. The use of technology in the preparations reflects Shenzhen's broader strengths in innovation and manufacturing. Xia Lei, deputy director of the city's science and technology innovation bureau, said that Shenzhen's industry has long generated more than 30 percent of its GDP, helping to translate research findings in laboratories into market-ready products. He pointed to the Huaqiangbei electronics market and the city's extensive supply chains as part of the ecosystem in which technology businesses have grown. Shenzhen has given rise to global technology leaders including Huawei, BYD, Tencent and DJI. The city posted GDP of 3.87 trillion yuan ($580 billion) in 2025, with research and development spending reaching 7.1 percent of GDP — the highest ratio among Chinese cities for the second consecutive year. That industrial strength is underpinned by an extensive network of regional trade and investment. During the first nine months of 2026, trade with other APEC economies rose 40 percent year-on-year, accounting for nearly 70 percent of Shenzhen's total foreign trade. Shenzhen companies invested $4.1 billion in those economies, accounting for more than 60 percent of the city's outward investment volume, according to data-released at Saturday's briefing. The city has also become the first on the Chinese mainland to surpass 5 trillion yuan in foreign trade, with imports and exports reaching 5.25 trillion yuan in the first 10 months of 2026, according to customs data. Zhang Feimeng, director-general of Shenzhen's commerce bureau, said that imports reached 2.24 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, up 70.1 percent, as the city worked to open its market wider to overseas suppliers. Meanwhile, Shenzhen's combined exports of competitive products, such as 3D printers, digital cameras and smartphones, grew 15.5 percent during the same period. Ma Jiangtao, founding director of the Doctorate Association — a nonprofit organization based in the United Kingdom that connects global scholars for academic exchanges — said that a city's international character is built through genuine exchanges and tangible business opportunities. He expressed hope that continued opening-up would attract more international visitors to China, unlocking more opportunities for cooperation. Du Lan, deputy director of the China Institute of International Studies' Department for Asia-Pacific Studies, said that Shenzhen's use of technology and city services to welcome international guests signals a broader opportunity for China to support Asia-Pacific growth through market openness and innovation cooperation. China can leverage its vast market to offer businesses more predictable market access by promoting trade and investment liberalization and closer alignment with regional trade arrangements, Du said. Contact the writers at zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Why 'big nose' US boy still calls China home
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Three tiles embedded in the ground near the doorway to David Plymire's home in the United States bear Chinese characters. They read, fu (good fortune), heping (peace) and xi (joy). Plymire is an American, but in a small town in northwestern China, there is a children's rhyme about him. For generations, children in Huangyuan, Qinghai province, on the eastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau, have recited a comical story about the "big nose" American boy. Until recently, few people knew that the child it describes was a real person, who is now 95 and living thousands of kilometers away across the Pacific. "An American with a big nose who loves Chinese niangpizi (cold spicy noodles)," Plymire said, reciting the children's poem in a recent interview with China Daily. "Then the big nose goes to the river to wash the pepper out of his nose, and he falls in the river and drowns." Plymire chuckled at the image. On the northern outskirts of Springfield, Missouri, the birthplace of America's famous Route 66, Plymire lives in a retirement community. He speaks fluent Mandarin as well as the local dialect of Huangyuan, where he spent 17 years of his early life. He has returned to China more than 20 times, raising money for medical equipment and helping improve healthcare in the town he still calls home. The childhood rhyme, now circulating online, has introduced his story to a new generation of Chinese, many young enough to be his great-grandchildren.

item.title: Why does skyscraper-studded Shenzhen draw migratory birds year after year?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Every autumn and winter, large numbers of migratory birds arrive in Shenzhen, either to rest over the winter or pass through on their journeys. What makes this modern metropolis such a reliable, welcoming stop for these avian travelers returning like clockwork each year? China Daily reporter Yan An ventured into the mangrove forests of Shenzhen Bay with Zhang Gaofeng, secretary-general of the Shenzhen Bird Watching Society, to find the answer. During the 2026 APEC "China Year", China and Asia-Pacific economies continue to deepen green cooperation, jointly address ecological and environmental challenges and safeguard regional ecological security and biodiversity. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will take place in Shenzhen from Nov 18 to 19. Stay tuned to see how this gathering will advance more cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region.

item.title: Striding in Sync
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Growing up in Sydney and now building a career in Shenzhen, Laurie Pearcey's life is the story of a cross-border bond forged across ocean expanses. In Sydney he met his Chinese wife; in Shenzhen he has embraced the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and all it has to offer. Beyond personal ties, deep-rooted links in education, trade and technology — from laser innovation to drone applications — unite people and industries in both cities. With Shenzhen hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, this mutual engagement highlights openness, innovation and cooperation — the three priorities of the 2026 APEC "China Year". APEC was established in Australia in 1989, since when member economies have striven to improve the prosperity of their peoples.

item.title: CEO summit to fuel integration
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
Deepening regional economic integration, advancing free trade and expanding innovation cooperation will be crucial to unlocking new growth opportunities across the Asia-Pacific, as business leaders and policymakers sought to build a more connected and dynamic regional economy. In a sign of the region's commitment to closer cooperation, 12 leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation member economies will attend the APEC CEO Summit 2026, which is scheduled to be held on Tuesday and Wednesday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade announced on Sunday. President Xi Jinping, along with leaders from APEC economies Australia, Canada, Chile, China's Hong Kong, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam, will attend the summit and deliver speeches or remarks, or will take part in panel discussions, said Li Qingshuang, the council's vice-chairwoman, at a news conference. Li said business leaders from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies will attend the APEC CEO Summit 2026, with companies from the United States accounting for nearly 20 percent of participating businesses, the largest share among economies outside the Chinese mainland. Ahead of the summit, during the opening ceremony of the fourth meeting of the APEC Business Advisory Council in Shenzhen on Saturday, representatives from APEC economies called for greater openness and cooperation to deepen regional economic integration, improve connectivity and advance digital innovation. Participants from Singapore, Thailand, Mexico, New Zealand and the US emphasized the importance of sustained dialogue and closer business engagement in navigating an increasingly complex international economic environment. More than 200 representatives and guests from 21 APEC economies have gathered in Shenzhen for the meeting, which is scheduled to conclude on Monday, according to a statement released by the CCPIT over the weekend. Li Fanrong, 2026 chair of the APEC Business Advisory Council and chairman of State-owned Sinochem Holdings Corp, said the council has identified 14 key deliverables this year, including policy recommendations to APEC leaders and statements addressing regional economic integration, free trade and connectivity. Loreto Leyton, a business advisory council representative from Chile, said APEC remains one of the few platforms capable of bringing world leaders together for dialogue, playing an increasingly important role in promoting mutual understanding, cooperation and shared prosperity amid global challenges. She also pointed to opportunities to promote sustainability, facilitate trade in goods and services, and provide greater support for small and medium-sized enterprises. Kok Ping Soon, a business advisory council representative from Singapore, said: "For Singapore, trade rules are our lifeline. They create a level playing field for businesses and people, making deeper regional integration and a modernized global trading system essential." The APEC Business Advisory Council provides a platform for business leaders across the Asia-Pacific to offer policy recommendations to APEC leaders, drawing on their firsthand experience to ensure that proposals reflect market realities and the needs of companies across the region. Liu Chenyang, director of Nankai University's APEC Study Center in Tianjin, said the message from the meeting is clear: Asia-Pacific cooperation can deliver tangible benefits for economies of all sizes by translating policy commitments into new trade opportunities and building a more connected, inclusive regional economy. Aravind Yarlagadda, senior vice-president of industrial solutions at Baker Hughes Co, a US energy equipment manufacturer, said that China plays a pivotal role in connecting industrial supply chains across the Asia-Pacific region, offering opportunities for US companies to combine advanced technologies with Chinese manufacturing capabilities and expertise. Backed by six plants in China, Baker Hughes sees growing potential for cooperation in industrial artificial intelligence, predictive maintenance and energy efficiency, he said. Saravoot Yoovidhya, CEO of TCP Group, the Thai conglomerate behind the energy drink brand Red Bull, said China's commitment to high-level opening-up and its extensive trade ties across the Asia-Pacific region have positioned the country as a key driver of regional economic integration, industrial cooperation and supply chain connectivity. With cumulative investment exceeding 4.36 billion yuan ($653.5 million) in China, TCP is leveraging its manufacturing bases in Sichuan province and the Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region to deepen industrial cooperation and expand connectivity with other APEC economies. Jiang Xueqing contributed to this story.
